pr_title: usb: Enable USB by the application.
pr_body:
The only reasonable solution right now to address #27071 is forcing the application to manually enable USB subsystem.
This patch updates remaining samples (not included in #20375) to call `usb_enable()` in `main`.

@markus-becker-tridonic-com please review the sample You added recently (last commit). I don't know what was expected to be on usb-cdc but right now I can see some garbage output (with master as well).
Furthermore:
- the sample has several Kconfig warnings that could be addressed (both overlays & without any).
- The sample builds with warnings when `overlay-tri-n4m-br.conf` applied (`-Wunused-varaible`).

Fixes: #27071
pr_comments:
I wonder if there are other places outside of `samples/` where we need to enable USB manually now. For example:
https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/blob/master/soc/arm/atmel_sam0/common/bossa.c#L46

cc @nzmichaelh

> Although technically you are not changing an API, you should still add a note to the release notes that explains the change and describes how to adapt to it.

I believe You are refering to f7d166bc75. Tbh I am not 100% convinced We should introduce new API for checking if console is ready, same thing could be achieved by calling `uart_line_ctrl_get(dev, UART_LINE_CTRL_DTR, &dtr);` but the user must then get binding of the device. The addition I made is addressing @pabigot suggestion [comment](https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/issues/27071#issuecomment-665574602).

I let that go and I am waiting for opinions.

This addition requires users to `#include <drivers/console/uart_console.h>`.
If the app wishes to use more line controls (Kconfig option) like `UART_LINE_CTRL_BAUD_RATE` it will have to `#include <drivers/uart.h>` in addition and call `uart_line_ctrl_get(dev, control, &ret);`

Furthermore as pointed by @pabigot in #27160 it seems that not only DTR is the the thing we should wait for to say: "hey, Your console is ready now". I had just a brief look into that and  there is one suspect but didn't have time to investage any further.

> Although technically you are not changing an API, you should still add a note to the release notes that explains the change and describes how to adapt to it.

After a rethink I brought back changes to `tracing_backend.h`. I believe there is no point to add `*_is_ready` API function. The only change I made is check if `init` function exists prior to calling it and this I included in the release notes.

> I wonder if there are other places outside of `samples/` where we need to enable USB manually now. For example:
> https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/blob/master/soc/arm/atmel_sam0/common/bossa.c#L46
> 
> cc @nzmichaelh

I don't think I can do something about that. The Kconfig option for bossa bootloader says:
```
Signifies that the target uses a BOSSA compatible bootloader.  If CDC
ACM USB support is also enabled then the board will reboot into the
bootloader automatically when bossac is run.
```

I assume once user enabled CDC ACM alongside bossa bootloader he/she will need to enable the USB subsystem as described in API notes.

> I believe You are refering to [f7d166b](https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/commit/f7d166bc7570184976ebf28127e6d393d29b068b). Tbh I am not 100% convinced We should introduce new API for checking if console is ready, same thing could be achieved by calling `uart_line_ctrl_get(dev, UART_LINE_CTRL_DTR, &dtr);` but the user must then get binding of the device. The addition I made is addressing @pabigot suggestion [comment](https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/issues/27071#issuecomment-665574602).

No no, I was referring to the fact that you now need to call `usb_enable()` manually even if using cdc acm or other classes. This should definitely be in the release notes, because it forces the user to modify their application in order to achieve the same result. We should list the cases and Kconfig options that now require enabling USB from the app, and that before did not.

> No no, I was referring to the fact that you now need to call `usb_enable()` manually even if using cdc acm or other classes. 

Users have been required to invoke `usb_enable()` explicitly since 2.2 was released.  That there were exceptions was an error.  I agree that it should be noted in the release notes that more applications will need to change (and note the resulting increased impact on lossage from USB console due to it starting later).

> I assume once user enabled CDC ACM alongside bossa bootloader he/she will need to enable the USB subsystem as described in API notes.

The callback for bossa allows USB to be used like a reset button.  AFAIK the boot loader doesn't need USB, or if it does it can enable it.  Also as long as the CDC ACM device can be obtained at the point the callback is registered it shouldn't matter whether at that point the device is ready to be used as a console.

(I don't know if the CDC ACM device pointer can be obtained before the device initializes; USB and normal devices may be different that way.)

I haven't had a chance to look at the implementation here; I will try to do so early this week.

> I do think we need a `cdc_acm_uart_ready()` API function and that the examples should use it. The console in particular will not work well if material gets output before it's ready.
> 
> IMO it shouldn't be `uart_console_ready()` because it's not generic to uart, and it's not specific to console. It is generic to CDC_ACM.

By this patch I don't want to address the #27160 but just make `usb_enable()` be called across all the samples that use USB.

All other comments are addressed.

> Although technically you are not changing an API, you should still add a note to the release notes that explains the change and describes how to adapt to it.

I've made a note to `release-notes-2.4.rst` file.

issue_context.title: USB: CDC-ACM uart console hijacks usb_enable call preventing user applications from registering callbacks
issue_context.body:
The UART console driver, when associated with USB_CDC_ACM device via `CONFIG_USB_UART_CONSOLE`, improperly invokes `usb_enable(NULL)` although that function is documented to be under the control of the application, which may want to provide a callback.

This has been true "forever", but became more visible due to #25894 which causes the call to `usb_enable()` to be invoked for the console even when `CONFIG_USB_UART_DTR_WAIT` is not selected.

There are two concerns exposed by this behavior:

* First, as long as `usb_enable()` includes this requirement:

      * Class-specific initialization and registration must be performed by the user
      * before invoking this, so that any data or events on the bus are processed
      * correctly by the associated class handling code.

  then drivers should not be invoking it unconditionally if their doing so prevents the user from ensuring this initialization is performed in the right order.  (It may be that it doesn't prevent this, but that's certainly not obvious. and the obvious alternative solution of initialization in `SYS_INIT()` is not consistent with how this would be done if the application did not select `CONFIG_USB_UART_CONSOLE=y` and instead invoked `usb_enable()` from main or some other application context.)

* Second, it's not obvious that the correct decision when the console device can't be opened is to cause the application to busy-wait until USB becomes available, even if `WAIT_FOR_DTR` is selected.

The same issue applies to #26122 which proposes to add another situation where the infrastructure, rather than the application, is invoking `usb_enable()`.

It's not immediately clear how this should can be resolved.  One question is whether for non-USB-UART console devices failure to initialize causes the application to hang.  If so, then changing this may be harder to justify.

If not, then perhaps the console could left in a dormant neutral state until something signals that USB (and possibly DTR) becomes available.  Transitioning out of that state would require the UART console driver to be notified when these conditions are met, something that can be signaled only by the USB subsystem.
comments: @pabigot That title is a better description of the problem.

> There are a couple other things that might be helpful with regard to the DTR functionality of the startup.

Please open an issue for that.  It's not something that'd be addressed here.  (I haven't noticed that need, myself.)
It can be done in the application.  I thought I would mention it in case you found it useful.
`netusb`, `tracing`, and `openthread/platform/uart` all try to enable USB without coordination also.

And  why does USB have to be initialized at application runlevel?  (Rhetorical question.)

> This is our preferred solution at this point.

OK, just make very clear that using a USB console (which is not optional on some platforms) means any pre-APPLICATION log messages will be dropped (which is very much not ideal; I'm going to have to look into non-console log destinations).

I do like that this path allows removal of `USB_UART_DTR_WAIT` which is either badly named or mis-implemented as it only (ever?) applied to a console UART.

I do not, though, believe that applications should be forced to implement that magic check.  It should be abstracted to a function `uart_console_wait_until_ready()` which would ideally delegate to `cdc_acm_wait_for_dtr()` which would do the magic.  (`uart_console_wait_until_ready()` should return `-ENOTSUP` for non-USB consoles.)

Also (reminder to self): the Kconfig help for `USB_UART_CONSOLE` needs to be updated to make much more clear what functionality selecting it does and does not affect.

> Also don't lose sight of [the other places](https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/issues/27071#issuecomment-662679087) that might be breaking the API.

I am working on PR adding this. In case of any doubts will post a message. We talked about the issue together with USB folks and that's the only way out we see for now.
